title: Kubernetes
label: K8s
desc: Declarative container orchestration: pods, workloads, networking and the kubectl commands that inspect them.

sections.title: Setup
sections.description: Install the client, point it at a cluster and confirm it answers.

snippets.code:
# Client build and the API server behind the current context
kubectl version --client
kubectl cluster-info

# Local clusters: kind for CI-shaped tests, minikube for a full node
kind create cluster --name cheatrs
minikube start --driver=docker --kubernetes-version=v1.32.0

# Completion and a shorter alias for the rest of the session
eval "$(kubectl completion bash)"
alias k=kubectl

# Apply a manifest and block until the pod reports Ready
kubectl apply -f pod.yaml
kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready pod/web --timeout=90s

# Everything the client can list in the current namespace
kubectl get all

sections.title: Contexts
sections.description: Contexts bundle a cluster, a user and a namespace; switching is one command.

snippets.code:
# Every context in the kubeconfig, with the active one marked
kubectl config get-contexts
kubectl config current-context

# Switch cluster, then pin the default namespace of this context
kubectl config use-context kind-cheatrs
kubectl config set-context --current --namespace=staging

# A specific kubeconfig file for one command
KUBECONFIG=/home/felipe/.kube/prod.yaml kubectl get nodes

# Rename a context after importing it
kubectl config rename-context kind-cheatrs local

# Merge two files into one; the colon separates them on Linux and macOS
KUBECONFIG=dev.yaml:prod.yaml kubectl config view --flatten -o yaml > merged.yaml

sections.title: Pods
sections.description: The smallest unit: one or more containers scheduled together on a node.

snippets.code:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: web
  labels:
    app: web
spec:
  containers:
    - name: web
      image: nginx:1.27-alpine
      ports:
        - containerPort: 80

# Throwaway pod with a shell, deleted on exit
kubectl run shell --rm -it --image=busybox:1.36 -- sh

# Node, pod IP and restart count, then the events at the bottom of describe
kubectl get pods -o wide
kubectl describe pod web

# Generate the manifest instead of typing it, then keep it in git
kubectl run web --image=nginx:1.27-alpine --port=80 --dry-run=client -o yaml > pod.yaml
kubectl apply -f pod.yaml

sections.title: Deployments
sections.description: Declare a replica count and an image; the controller keeps reality matching it.

snippets.code:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: web
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: web
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: web
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: web
          image: nginx:1.27-alpine
          ports:
            - containerPort: 80

kubectl scale deployment web --replicas=5
kubectl set image deployment/web web=nginx:1.28-alpine
kubectl rollout status deployment/web

kubectl get deployments
kubectl get pods -l app=web -o wide
kubectl describe deployment web

sections.title: Services
sections.description: Give a stable virtual IP and DNS name to a changing set of pods.

snippets.code:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: web
spec:
  type: ClusterIP
  selector:
    app: web
  ports:
    - name: http
      port: 80
      targetPort: 80

# Expose a deployment without writing YAML; ClusterIP is the default
kubectl expose deployment web --name=web --port=80 --target-port=80

# NodePort for a quick check from the host, LoadBalancer on a cloud
kubectl expose deployment web --name=web-nodeport --type=NodePort --port=80

kubectl get services,endpoints

sections.title: Ingress
sections.description: Route external HTTP by host and path to Services, with TLS in front.

snippets.code:
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: web
  annotations:
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/rewrite-target: /
spec:
  ingressClassName: nginx
  rules:
    - host: web.local
      http:
        paths:
          - path: /
            pathType: Prefix
            backend:
              service:
                name: web
                port:
                  number: 80

# The controller that serves the nginx ingress class
helm upgrade --install ingress-nginx ingress-nginx \
  --repo https://kubernetes.github.io/ingress-nginx \
  --namespace ingress-nginx --create-namespace

kubectl get ingress
kubectl describe ingress web

apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: web-tls
spec:
  ingressClassName: nginx
  tls:
    - hosts:
        - web.local
      secretName: web-tls
  rules:
    - host: web.local
      http:
        paths:
          - path: /
            pathType: Prefix
            backend:
              service:
                name: web
                port:
                  number: 80

sections.title: ConfigMaps and Secrets
sections.description: Keep configuration out of the image and inject it as env or files.

snippets.code:
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: app-config
data:
  LOG_LEVEL: info
  APP_PORT: "8080"
  config.yaml: |
    retries: 3
    timeout_seconds: 15

apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: db-credentials
type: Opaque
stringData:
  POSTGRES_USER: app_user
  POSTGRES_PASSWORD: devsecret

apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: api
spec:
  containers:
    - name: api
      image: busybox:1.36
      command: ["sh", "-c", "env | sort; sleep 3600"]
      envFrom:
        - configMapRef:
            name: app-config
        - secretRef:
            name: db-credentials

sections.title: Volumes
sections.description: Share files between containers or survive a pod restart.

snippets.code:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: cache
spec:
  containers:
    - name: app
      image: busybox:1.36
      command: ["sh", "-c", "while true; do date >> /cache/heartbeat; sleep 5; done"]
      volumeMounts:
        - name: cache
          mountPath: /cache
  volumes:
    - name: cache
      emptyDir:
        sizeLimit: 64Mi

apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: data
spec:
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteOnce
  storageClassName: standard
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 5Gi

apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: db
spec:
  containers:
    - name: postgres
      image: postgres:17
      volumeMounts:
        - name: data
          mountPath: /var/lib/postgresql/data
  volumes:
    - name: data
      persistentVolumeClaim:
        claimName: data

sections.title: Resources
sections.description: Requests decide scheduling, limits decide who gets throttled or killed.

snippets.code:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: api
spec:
  containers:
    - name: api
      image: nginx:1.27-alpine
      resources:
        requests:
          cpu: 100m
          memory: 128Mi
        limits:
          cpu: 500m
          memory: 256Mi

apiVersion: v1
kind: LimitRange
metadata:
  name: defaults
spec:
  limits:
    - type: Container
      default:
        cpu: 500m
        memory: 256Mi
      defaultRequest:
        cpu: 100m
        memory: 128Mi

# What the node reserved, then what the containers actually use
kubectl describe node kind-cheatrs-control-plane | sed -n '/Allocated resources/,/Events/p'
kubectl top pods
kubectl top nodes

sections.title: Probes
sections.description: Startup, readiness and liveness answer three different questions.

snippets.code:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: api
spec:
  containers:
    - name: api
      image: nginx:1.27-alpine
      ports:
        - containerPort: 80
      startupProbe:
        httpGet:
          path: /
          port: 80
        failureThreshold: 30
        periodSeconds: 2
      readinessProbe:
        httpGet:
          path: /
          port: 80
        periodSeconds: 5
      livenessProbe:
        httpGet:
          path: /
          port: 80
        periodSeconds: 10
        failureThreshold: 3

apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: cache
spec:
  containers:
    - name: redis
      image: redis:7.4-alpine
      ports:
        - containerPort: 6379
      readinessProbe:
        exec:
          command: ["redis-cli", "ping"]
        periodSeconds: 5
      livenessProbe:
        tcpSocket:
          port: 6379
        periodSeconds: 10

# Probe failures surface as Unhealthy events and a climbing restart count
kubectl describe pod api | sed -n '/Containers:/,/Events:/p'
kubectl get pod api -o jsonpath='{.status.containerStatuses[0].restartCount}'

sections.title: Logs and Debug
sections.description: Read stdout from the container, the previous one, or the whole workload.

snippets.code:
kubectl logs web-7d9c8b6f5-2xk4p
kubectl logs -f deployment/web --tail=100
kubectl logs web-7d9c8b6f5-2xk4p -c sidecar

# The container that crashed, before the restart
kubectl logs web-7d9c8b6f5-2xk4p --previous

# Every pod of a selector at once, each line prefixed with its pod
kubectl logs -l app=web --all-containers --prefix --tail=50

# Cluster events by time: the first place to look when a pod is stuck
kubectl get events --sort-by=.lastTimestamp
kubectl get events --field-selector involvedObject.name=web-7d9c8b6f5-2xk4p

sections.title: Exec and Port-forward
sections.description: Get a shell, copy a file, or reach a Service from the laptop.

snippets.code:
# Interactive shell, then a one-off command in the same container
kubectl exec -it web-7d9c8b6f5-2xk4p -- sh
kubectl exec web-7d9c8b6f5-2xk4p -- nginx -v

# Copy files out without a shell in the image
kubectl cp web-7d9c8b6f5-2xk4p:/etc/nginx/nginx.conf ./nginx.conf

# Local 8080 to the Service on 80, no Ingress or NodePort needed
kubectl port-forward service/web 8080:80

# Straight to a pod, backgrounded for a curl test
kubectl port-forward pod/web-7d9c8b6f5-2xk4p 8081:80 &
curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:8081/

# Distroless image: attach an ephemeral container that has a shell
kubectl debug -it web-7d9c8b6f5-2xk4p --image=busybox:1.36 --target=web

sections.title: Namespaces
sections.description: Split one cluster into virtual scopes for teams and environments.

snippets.code:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: staging
  labels:
    env: staging

kubectl create namespace staging
kubectl get namespaces
kubectl delete namespace staging

# Make staging the default for this context, no -n per command
kubectl config set-context --current --namespace=staging

# Scope one command, or look everywhere at once
kubectl get pods -n kube-system
kubectl get pods --all-namespaces

sections.title: Jobs and CronJobs
sections.description: Run work that finishes, once or on a schedule.

snippets.code:
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: migrate
spec:
  backoffLimit: 3
  ttlSecondsAfterFinished: 600
  template:
    spec:
      restartPolicy: Never
      containers:
        - name: migrate
          image: postgres:17
          command: ["psql", "-c", "SELECT 1"]

apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: backup
spec:
  schedule: "0 3 * * *"
  concurrencyPolicy: Forbid
  successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 3
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
          containers:
            - name: backup
              image: postgres:17
              command: ["pg_dumpall", "--file=/backup/all.sql"]

kubectl get jobs
kubectl logs job/migrate

# Trigger a CronJob now without waiting for the schedule
kubectl create job --from=cronjob/backup backup-manual

sections.title: Rollouts
sections.description: Watch, pause, undo and restart a Deployment without hand-editing pods.

snippets.code:
kubectl rollout status deployment/web
kubectl rollout history deployment/web
kubectl rollout history deployment/web --revision=3

# Undo the last rollout, or a specific revision
kubectl rollout undo deployment/web
kubectl rollout undo deployment/web --to-revision=2

# Recreate every pod without touching the image
kubectl rollout restart deployment/web

# The change-cause annotation is what rollout history shows
kubectl annotate deployment/web kubernetes.io/change-cause="image nginx:1.28-alpine"

# Freeze a rollout mid-way to inspect, then let it finish
kubectl rollout pause deployment/web
kubectl rollout resume deployment/web

sections.title: Common Errors
sections.description: The four states that stop a pod, and the command that explains each one.

snippets.code:
# CrashLoopBackOff: read the exit code and the log of the dead container
kubectl describe pod web-7d9c8b6f5-2xk4p | sed -n '/Last State/,/Events:/p'
kubectl logs web-7d9c8b6f5-2xk4p --previous

# ImagePullBackOff: the node cannot pull, check the tag and the registry secret
kubectl describe pod web-7d9c8b6f5-2xk4p | grep -A3 "Failed"
kubectl get secret regcred -o jsonpath='{.type}'

# Pending: no node fits the requests, the event says which resource ran out
kubectl describe pod web-7d9c8b6f5-2xk4p | sed -n '/Events:/,$p'

# OOMKilled: the container crossed its memory limit and was killed
kubectl get pod web-7d9c8b6f5-2xk4p \
  -o jsonpath='{.status.containerStatuses[0].lastState.terminated.reason}'
